subject: Redwood + AcmeCloud discovery — integration recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood + AcmeCloud discovery — integration recap & next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared:
- High embedding/re-ranking costs and unpredictable latency when running at scale (esp. tail latency for multi-turn chat).
- Need to support streaming responses into your product UI (low-latency partial tokens) rather than waiting for full completion.
- Desire for structured outputs (JSON events) to drive downstream workflows and analytics; current LLM outputs are too free-form for your pipeline.
- Security/compliance: logs retention, audit trails, and option for Private (VPC) deployment for regulated datasets.

Goals we agreed on:
- Target end-to-end user latency for chat scenarios: <= 200ms p50, predictable tail behavior.
- Proof-of-concept (POC) to validate embedding-based reranking and streaming chat integration with up to 10k concurrent users in a sandbox.
- Provide a deployment option (Hosted or Private) with clear SLAs and data controls.

Integration / product fit notes (technical summary):
- SDK: You will call Redwood SDK from your platform. SDK changes required on your side: support for streaming client (we provide websocket and streaming HTTP client libs), and a small client change to accept function-calling hooks for structured outputs.
- Function calling: We recommend using function-call schema for the top-level intent extraction and for emitting structured JSON events that your backend can consume (we’ll share example schemas).
- Streaming: Redwood supports chunked token streaming; we’ll provide a sample streaming handler for your React UI to minimize perceived latency.
- Structured outputs: Use the SDK function-calling or our structured-output mode to get stable JSON shapes (easier for downstream ETL).
- Embeddings/re-ranking: We suggest a pipeline where you store sparse/reduced-dim vectors (we suggest 1536 dims) and use Redwood embeddings + reranker for candidate scoring. We can run a small benchmark during the POC to tune vector dims and quantization level to balance cost and accuracy.

Attachments included: Redwood_Integration_Playbook_v1.pdf (high-level architecture + SDK examples), POC_scope_acme.xlsx (proposed success criteria & timeline), SOW_draft_acme.docx (commercial starting point).

Immediate next steps:
1) I’ll share the integration playbook and POC scope (attached) — please confirm the success criteria in the spreadsheet by EOD Friday.
2) Can you share a small sample of the dataset (anonymized) and 2-3 example UI flows where streaming/structured output matters?
3) Proposed timeline: kickoff next Monday 01/18, 3-week technical POC, follow-up evaluation with engineers and product.

I’ve looped Rishi and Neha from our Solutions and Product teams to help with technical scoping and success criteria. Demos and baseline benchmarks will be led by Dylan (cc’d on follow-ups).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Redwood + AcmeCloud discovery — integration recap & next steps

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough recap — this looks right. A few clarifications/questions from our side:

1) Embedding dims: 1536 sounds reasonable; curious if you have guidance on 768 vs 1536 vs 3072 tradeoffs for reranking accuracy vs cost.
2) Tail latency: our primary concern is p99 for multi-turn sessions. Can you call out expected p99 for the model config you recommend?
3) Data sharing: we can put together an anonymized sample dataset and two UI flows by Thursday. Do you have a preferred secure upload (SFTP or Drive with limited access)?

We’re aligned on the POC timeline, but want to confirm the expected Redwood engineering time commitment during the 3-week POC (weekly checkpoints + one on-site/remote demo at week 3).

Also looping in Maya (CTO) to keep leadership in the loop.

Best,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering, AcmeCloud
alex.johnson@acmecloud.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 15:58:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood + AcmeCloud discovery — integration recap & next steps

Alex — great questions. Short answers below; Dylan will add technical detail in a follow-up:

1) Embedding dims: 1536 is a common sweet spot for reranking; 768 can be slightly cheaper but may require more retrieval candidates; 3072 yields higher fidelity but increases storage/cost ~2x. We’ll include a small benchmark in the POC to pick the right tradeoff for your dataset.
2) Tail latency: For the model/quantization profile we expect p50 ~40–80ms and p99 ~200–350ms for single-request reranking (depending on batch size and hardware). For streaming chat with function calling, p99 can be higher — we’ll optimize with KV-cache and batching rules as part of the POC.
3) Secure upload: Drive link is OK for initial samples (use restricted link); for sensitive data we can provide SFTP + short-lived credentials. I created a restricted Drive folder and put the playbook there (link below).

POC engineering commitment: Redwood will allocate a Solutions Engineer (Dylan) ~0.5 FTE during the 3-week POC (weekly 60-min checkpoints + final demo). Product engagement from Neha on success criteria and metrics. Commercial/contracting will be minimal but we’ll put the SOW draft as a starting point.

Can you confirm you’ll share the anonymized dataset by Thursday? Once we have that we’ll run an initial embedding/re-ranking baseline and share results in week 1.

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cREDWOOD-integration-playbook

Thanks — Marissa

Hey Alex / team —

Thanks for the notes. A few concrete technical items from my side to make the POC smooth:

- Function calling / structured outputs: I’ll attach two example JSON schemas we recommend (intent_event.json, search_result.json) and a short example of how the SDK maps model output -> structured payload using function calls. This avoids brittle parsing on your side.

- Streaming: We support both websocket streaming and streaming HTTP. For your React UI the websocket approach will give the smallest latency spikes. I’ll share a sample streaming handler (JS) that wires partial token updates to the UI and emits final structured events when the function call completes.

- Embeddings/reranking: Start with 1536 dims using Redwood embeddings. For storage we recommend productized PQ / quantization (we’ll run 8-bit and 4-bit quant benchmarks for recall/latency tradeoffs). Please send a ~1k record anonymized set so we can run the initial benchmark (embedding speed, similarity recall, rerank accuracy).

- Metrics we’ll capture during POC: p50/p95/p99 latency for chat and rerank endpoints, tokens-per-second throughput, cost per 1k reranks, and rerank precision@5 on your test set.

Action items (from Dylan):
1) Alex — upload anonymized dataset (1k samples) to the Drive folder by Thu 01/14.
2) Alex — share two example UI flows/screenshots where streaming/structured outputs are expected.
3) Redwood — I’ll drop the example schemas and sample SDK snippets in the Drive folder and schedule the first checkpoint for Mon 01/18 (time TBD).

If you prefer SFTP for the dataset, send a point-of-contact and we’ll provide creds.

Will follow up with the small attachments and quick code snippets.

—Dylan
